newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli tax revenues rise one pct in three months.
newsitem.headline: Israeli tax revenues rise one pct in three months.

text.p: Israeli government tax revenues and other fees rose only one percent after inflation in the three months to January 31 from the year-earlier period to approximately 25 billion shekels, the Treasury said on Monday.
After taking into account changes to the tax code, revenues fell 0.7 percent, the ministry added.
The Treasury did not release separate figures for January.

Revenues from income and property tax in November-January rose about one percent after inflation from a year earlier to 13.1 billion shekels but 1.4 percent after adjusting for changes to the tax code.

Revenues from customs and the value-added tax were also up about one percent to 11.4 billion shekels but only 0.3 percent after taking into account tax-code changes, the Treasury said. It said tax revenues on imports fell a real 17 percent following a sharp drop in imports of consumer durables. The fall was offset by higher taxes on petrol and cigarettes that went into effect January 1.
